description: 2-adic parity split of the exact D-ladder: does separating even-k/odd-k coefficient subseries resolve the q-Gevrey 'no single Gevrey index' into two fixed-order Borel-summable series?

data.verdict: PARTIAL — the physically-relevant half is clean. The **odd-k** subseries (bar-ODD = the S-carrier, i.e. the Q_β c₃ half) is fixed-order Borel–Leroy summable at a STABLE order s_B=0.068315 (drift 0.00346), MATCHING the independent merged log-fit divergence exponent C≈0.06; the **even-k** subseries still drifts (s_A=0.35537, drift 0.0234). NEW (this fresh-context finding): the merged combined-series 'no single Gevrey index' is **even-k-driven** — the even half's drift contaminates the combined estimator, while the physically-relevant ODD (S-carrier) half has a clean fixed order. The root-test/log-fit disagreement of the combined scan (s*≈0.20 vs C≈0.06) is thus a parity-mixing artifact; the odd half sits at ≈0.068 by BOTH estimators. Actionable for the Écalle builders (#3683/#3805): resum the odd (S-carrier) half at fixed Borel–Leroy order ≈0.068 rather than the drifting combined series; only the even half needs full acceleration. Scope-(a) measurement; no c_k wired; no fit; no tier change.
